clinicalPearls: An X-linked disorder of males combining severe intellectual disability with a mild form of alpha-thalassaemia
Characteristic facial features include a small triangular face with hypertelorism, epicanthic folds, a small nose with anteverted nares and a tented upper lip, giving a hypotonic facial appearance
Genital abnormalities such as cryptorchidism, hypospadias or ambiguous genitalia are common
Marked hypotonia, feeding difficulties, short stature and skeletal changes are frequent
The alpha-thalassaemia is usually mild and detected as haemoglobin H (HbH) inclusions in red cells on a specific stain
Caused by variants in ATRX, encoding a chromatin-remodelling helicase; carrier females are usually unaffected owing to skewed X-inactivation
The blood picture may be subtle, so HbH inclusions can be missed unless specifically sought
reference.pathophysiology: ATRX encodes a chromatin-remodelling ATPase of the helicase family that, in partnership with the histone chaperone DAXX, deposits the histone variant H3.3 at heterochromatic regions such as telomeres and, importantly, regulates expression of the alpha-globin gene cluster. Loss-of-function variants impair this chromatin regulation, reducing alpha-globin transcription (producing mild alpha-thalassaemia with HbH inclusions) and disrupting gene expression required for normal brain, genital and skeletal development. Because the gene is on the X chromosome, males are affected while carrier females are protected by skewed X-inactivation. The combined chromatin and globin dysregulation explains the coexistence of intellectual disability and a haematological abnormality.
additionalDifferentials: Disorders of sex development with intellectual disability
additionalInvestigations: Full blood count and peripheral film with a supravital stain for HbH inclusions
Haemoglobin analysis (electrophoresis or HPLC) noting that HbH may be low or absent
Assessment of genital and endocrine status
Targeted ATRX sequencing or an X-linked intellectual-disability gene panel or exome sequencing
redFlags: Feeding failure, aspiration or faltering growth in infancy
reference.prognosis: ATR-X syndrome causes lifelong severe intellectual disability with limited speech and independence; the alpha-thalassaemia is usually mild and rarely a major clinical problem. Care is supportive, addressing feeding, gastrointestinal, genital and developmental needs.
pitfalls: Missing the diagnosis because HbH inclusions are absent or not specifically sought
Attributing genital anomalies to an isolated disorder of sex development
Overlooking the diagnosis in a male with intellectual disability and hypotonic facies
Assuming carrier females will be affected
references: GeneReviews: Alpha-Thalassemia X-Linked Intellectual Disability Syndrome
management: Provide supportive, multidisciplinary care for the severe intellectual disability as there is no disease-specific therapy, with individualised special education and communication support
Address feeding difficulties with nutritional support and management of gastrointestinal problems such as reflux and constipation
Manage genital abnormalities with surgical correction of cryptorchidism or hypospadias and endocrine assessment as indicated
Support motor development and hypotonia with physiotherapy and occupational therapy
Monitor the usually mild alpha-thalassaemia with periodic full blood count, transfusion being rarely required

Coordinate care through clinical genetics, paediatrics and neurodevelopmental services, and offer genetic counselling for this X-linked disorder with carrier testing of female relatives and family screening
